votes.motion: Accept the minutes from the March 10, 2026 meeting

budget_items.topic: Manhole repair IFB / In Situ Technologies contract
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said the contractor still has roughly 10 to 15 manholes to line and about 15 more needing frame-and-cover replacement, expected to finish within about a month once cold weather breaks.
The business manager gave a ballpark cost per manhole for the cementitious liner used to seal them.
A commissioner estimated a discontinued 1.25-inch pump line was leaking roughly that much water per day into the sewer system, discovered while investigating an unrelated job.
The business manager said the commission is tight on funds at the end of the fiscal year, so a wider survey of manholes flagged in past studies cannot be done right now.

budget_items.topic: FY26 third quarter demands / delinquency rate
budget_items.what_was_said: Demands were sent out March 16 and people are starting to pay; the combined delinquency rate was described as around that figure, under 20%.

The board noted it already voted to approve the FY27 budget and an associated rate increase at a prior meeting; the town manager had follow-up questions but nothing changed, and it moves forward to town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Pawn Street sewer district connection request
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident/owner interested in joining the sewer district would need to pay for engineering plans before the board can vote on anything, and it is unclear if the owner wants to proceed given the cost.

budget_items.topic: Developer betterment for added sewer capacity (I&I offset)
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner described a practice used by other towns where a developer adding gallonage to the district must locate and fix an equivalent amount of leaking pipe capacity at their own expense.
The business manager said existing regulations already require developments above a certain size to eliminate I&I or pay a fee that goes into the district's I&I account.

decisions.decision: The DPW director will give the manhole-lining contractor the go-ahead to resume work once nighttime temperatures rise above freezing this week.
The leaking/discontinued manhole found on Laurel Lane will be added to In Situ Technologies' sealing work.
CTE's on-site inspector will change from Robert to Al Packer Jr. ('Elby'), as Robert is stepping back to focus on his own business.
Scott will give the budget presentation at town meeting.
The Pawn Street sewer district connection request stays on hold until the property owner decides whether to fund engineering plans.

minutes.headline: Sewer board finds major manhole water infiltration on Laurel Lane but can't fund a wider search this year
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission reviewed ongoing manhole-lining repairs, heard that a commissioner discovered a discontinued pump line pouring significant groundwater into the system on Laurel Lane, and discussed possibly requiring developers to offset added sewer capacity by fixing leaking pipes elsewhere. The FY27 budget and rate increase, already approved at a prior meeting, is moving to town meeting, and no further study of infiltration hotspots will happen this fiscal year due to tight funds.

what_happened.line: A commissioner found a discontinued pump line pouring groundwater into the sewer system on Laurel Lane, and the leak will be added to the contractor's sealing work.
The FY27 sewer budget and a rate increase, already approved at a prior meeting, moves forward to a town meeting vote.
The board said funds are too tight at fiscal year end to widen the search for other infiltration hot spots flagged in past studies.
The commission discussed a policy requiring developers who add sewer capacity to offset it by fixing an equivalent amount of leaking pipe elsewhere in town.
A resident's request to connect a Pawn Street property to the sewer district stays on hold pending the owner's decision on funding engineering plans.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked to vote on the FY27 sewer budget and rate increase at town meeting, which sets what sewer bills look like next year.
Groundwater leaking into the system through manholes and old pump lines adds to what the sewer system has to carry and treat, which is part of what any future rate increase would be paying to fix.
A developer offset requirement, if adopted, would shift some of the cost of fixing leaking infrastructure onto new development rather than existing ratepayers.
